hero.lead: A nation of 135.5 million on Africa’s great highland plateau, whose energy is almost entirely renewable and whose reform programme the IMF has backed with $3.4 billion.

capital.heading: Ethiopia runs one of Africa’s largest reform programmes. Next, a clean stove in every home.

register.text: A four-year programme behind the float of the birr and the restructuring of the nation’s debts.

register.name: Development Policy Operation
register.text: Backs the reforms that opened the economy to investment and stabilised prices.

register.name: Clean energy access (ASCENT Ethiopia)
register.text: Connects households, businesses and towns to the grid, aiming at six million people.

register.note: Short-term work for six million people

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 24 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A market square in an Ethiopian highland town

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Terraced green highland farmland and teff fields in Ethiopia

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Montane forest around an Ethiopian Orthodox church in the highlands

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: The Blue Nile Falls in the Ethiopian highlands

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2020
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile, wide view

items.name: The enterprises building Perfect Ethiopia
items.text: The Stewards are verifying the companies and social enterprises already delivering the seven basic living standards in Ethiopia. Suggest one to include.

coverage.gap_text: Ethiopians who cook without clean fuel or technology: 93 in every hundred.
